evals.name: 13b-on-80gb
evals.prompt: A100 80GB 한 장에 13B 모델을 bf16 + Adam으로 full fine-tuning 할 수 있어? 안 되면 batch size를 줄이면 될까?
evals.expected_output: No: model states are 16*Psi = 208 GB, independent of batch size, so lowering b cannot help. Lists ZeRO sharding, CPU offload, or PEFT as the routes.

assertions.description: Uses the 16Ψ (2+2+12) bytes-per-parameter model-state budget
Computes about 208 GB of model states for 13B
States explicitly that lowering batch size does NOT help because model states are independent of batch size
Offers concrete alternatives: sharding across GPUs with ZeRO, CPU offload of the optimizer, 8-bit optimizer, or PEFT/LoRA
Distinguishes full fine-tuning from LoRA/PEFT rather than answering 'yes' on the strength of PEFT

evals.name: oom-triage-order
evals.prompt: We're getting CUDA OOM in the forward pass. Someone suggested turning on gradient checkpointing. Is that the right first move?
evals.expected_output: Not first: selective recomputation (~2-5%) beats full recompute (~25-33%); before either, lower b and raise m (free) and use a fused attention kernel. Prices each rung.

assertions.description: Distinguishes selective activation recomputation (~2–5% overhead) from full recomputation (~25–33%) and prefers selective
Names cheaper prior steps such as lowering micro-batch b while raising m, or using a fused attention kernel
Attaches an explicit cost (percent step time or extra communication) to the options rather than listing them unpriced
Uses the fact that the OOM is in the forward pass to conclude the problem is activations rather than model states or optimizer state

evals.name: activation-memory-formula
evals.prompt: Give me the activation memory formula for one transformer layer, and tell me which term dominates at long sequence length.
evals.expected_output: s*b*h*(34 + 5as/h) bytes; the 5as/h attention term is quadratic in s and dominates; selective recompute removes exactly that term.

assertions.description: States the per-layer activation memory as s·b·h·(34 + 5as/h) bytes
Explains the 34 as attention block + MLP + layernorms, and the 5as/h as the attention score path
Identifies 5as/h as quadratic in s and therefore dominant at long sequence
Notes that selective recomputation removes exactly the 5as/h term, which is why it is so cheap for how much it saves

evals.name: fragmentation-signature
evals.prompt: OOM 에러에 'reserved memory is much greater than allocated memory'라고 나와. 메모리가 진짜 부족한 거야?
evals.expected_output: No — that is fragmentation: free bytes exist but no contiguous block. Recommends expandable_segments:True and uniform shapes; explains the caching allocator.

assertions.description: States this is fragmentation rather than a genuine shortage — there is free memory but no contiguous block large enough
Explains the caching allocator holds segments, so reserved minus allocated is memory paid for but unusable
Recommends expandable_segments:True (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF) as the primary fix
Suggests making tensor shapes uniform (padding/bucketing sequence lengths) as a cause and fix
Does not recommend calling empty_cache() inside the training loop, or explicitly warns against it

evals.name: offload-is-capability-not-performance
evals.prompt: 학습이 느려서 그런데, optimizer를 CPU로 offload하면 GPU 메모리가 늘어나니까 더 빨라질까?
evals.expected_output: No — offload is a capability tool, not a performance tool. PCIe is ~50x slower than HBM. It is the right thing to offload only because the optimizer step is low-AI and once per step.

assertions.description: States plainly that offload will not make training faster
Gives the bandwidth gap, e.g. PCIe ~64 GB/s versus HBM ~2000–3350 GB/s, roughly 30–50x
Uses the framing that offload is a capability tool that lets an otherwise-impossible model run
Explains why the optimizer is nonetheless the right thing to offload — low arithmetic intensity and touched once per step, unlike weights and activations

evals.name: more-gpus-under-ddp
evals.prompt: We hit OOM on 8 GPUs. Can we just add more nodes to get more memory?
evals.expected_output: Not under DDP — it replicates model states, so per-GPU memory is unchanged by n. Only sharding (ZeRO/TP/PP) converts world size into capacity.

assertions.description: States DDP replicates model states so per-GPU memory does not change with world size
Says only sharding — ZeRO stages, tensor parallelism, or pipeline parallelism — converts more GPUs into more capacity
Recommends a specific sharding route such as ZeRO-2 or ZeRO-3/FSDP
Notes ZeRO shards model states but not activations, so a ZeRO-3 job can still OOM inside a forward pass
